title: Lease-anchoring eviction invariants for prefetch-aware KV cache
creator: Aisha Marquez
description: Problem: Continuous batching + aggressive prefetching and GPU memory pressure have exposed non-deterministic evictions that violate prefix coherence guarantees. Currently we see rare cases where a prefetched KV segment is reclaimed while an in-flight batch still expects it, causing model decode divergence and increased latency due to repeated recomputation. Goal: specify and implement a lease-anchoring eviction protocol that (1) preserves prefix-level correctness across concurrent batches, (2) bounds GPU memory usage with predictable reclamation, and (3) composes with existing TTL/LRU heuristics for cold items.
acceptance_criteria: Formal invariant doc that states: if a batch references KV prefix P with lease L then no eviction that removes entries necessary to decode P can occur while L is active
Implementation of lease tokens (lease anchor + epoch) in KV store API and runtime: leases obtainable by continuous-batching scheduler and released deterministically
Unit and property-based tests that reproduce previous divergence scenarios and show zero failures across 1000 randomized seeds

Microbench: median token generation latency under typical workmix increases by <= 3% and 95th percentile by <= 8% compared to baseline without leasing; GPU memory footprint remains within planned watermark with <2% variance
Graceful fallback path: if lease allocation fails due to OOM, requests fallback to compatible model variant or run synchronous prefetch with backpressure instead of silent eviction
Documentation (Console and SDK) describing new lease semantics, observability keys, and cost implications
design_notes: Lease model: lightweight 64-bit token (epoch:32 bits + seq:32 bits). Anchors increment epoch on global reclamation cycles. Sequence ensures monotonic per-client ordering.

Anchoring semantics: continuous-batching scheduler acquires per-prefix anchors before issuing batch that may reference prefix KV. Anchor attaches to all prefetched segments and increments anchor refcount. Eviction checks require refcount==0 and anchor epoch matches current reclamation epoch.

Eviction policy composition: keep existing LRU/TTL scoring for candidate selection; require lease-anchoring and fence token checks to allow final reclamation. When anchor prevents eviction, mark candidate as "anchored-warm" to avoid repeated scanning.

Reclamation epochs: periodic epoch advance triggers a reconciliation pass to clear stale anchors whose owner did not explicitly release (safety against leaks). Leases include last-touch timestamp to help reconcile.
GPU memory optimization: use per-slab anchored bitmaps to avoid fine-grained atomic ops. Anchored slabs are tombstoned for reclamation but not freed until epoch reconciliation.

Failure modes: in rare anchor-leak cases, we will accept bounded memory pressure and trigger proactive canary draining (fallback to synchronous batching or model degrade) rather than inconsistent decode outputs.
Observability: expose lease_acquire/release events, epoch_advances, anchor_conflicts, and per-prefix anchor_refcount metrics in Console with taggable dimensions (model, region, route).

Compatibility: API changes are additive; SDKs receive helper calls for explicit anchor lifecycle but runtime will auto-anchor when using continuous-batching adapters. Backwards-compatible default: short-lived implicit anchors for non-continuous clients.
test_plan: Unit tests: anchor refcount increments/decrements under concurrent threads; eviction lookup rejects anchored slabs
Property tests: fuzzed sequences of prefetch, anchor, release, epoch_advance, eviction across 1000 seeds ensuring invariants hold
Integration: synthetic workload that mimics production mix (short-chat, long-chat, embeddings) to validate latency and memory signals
Stress: prolonged memory-pressure scenario with batch spike to validate epoch reconciliation does not drop correctness and triggers fallback
Benchmark: compare baseline runtime (no anchors) vs anchored runtime for token throughput and GPU memory fragmentation (slab utilization metrics)
Canary rollout plan: internal dedicated cluster -> prod-turbo ring -> global, with rollback toggles and telemetry gates
